title: Substrings of Size Three with Distinct Characters
spaceBreakdown:
- int count, int n, loop index i: scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no extra allocation
- not counted: input string s
approach: Iterate over every starting index i where a length-3 window fits (i from 0 to n-3). For each window s[i], s[i+1], s[i+2], it is good iff all three pairwise comparisons are unequal: s[i]≠s[i+1], s[i+1]≠s[i+2], and s[i]≠s[i+2]. Increment a counter when all three hold. With n ≤ 100 this is trivially O(n) and uses O(1) extra space.
hints: For any three characters, what is the minimum set of pairwise comparisons you must make to be certain none of them repeat?
Fixed-size sliding window of length 3. For s = "xyzzaz", window at i=0 is "xyz": x≠y, y≠z, x≠z → good; window at i=1 is "yzz": y≠z but z=z → not good.

```
count = 0
for i from 0 to n-3:
    a = s[i], b = s[i+1], c = s[i+2]
    if a != b and b != c and a != c:
        count = count + 1
return count
```

**Smallest input** - string shorter than 3 has no length-3 window
`Input: s = "ab"` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: loop bound `i < n` instead of `i + 2 < n` accesses s[i+2] out of range at i = n-1 → undefined behavior

**All equal** - every window contains a repeat
`Input: s = "aaaa"` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: checking only `s[i] != s[i+1] && s[i+1] != s[i+2]` (omitting `s[i] != s[i+2]`) → returns 0 here but gives wrong answer on "aba"

**First and last equal** - middle differs from both ends but ends match
`Input: s = "aba"` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the `s[i] != s[i+2]` comparison → returns 1 instead of 0

**Single good window** - exactly one valid substring
`Input: s = "abc"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: loop bound `i + 2 <= n` (using <= instead of <) → with n = 3 runs i = 0 and i = 1, reading s[3] out of range → wrong count

followUps.q: Generalize to count good substrings of length k (k ≤ n) where all k characters are distinct.
followUps.a: Slide a window of size k and maintain a frequency map of the characters currently inside it. A window is good exactly when the map size equals k. Add the incoming character, remove the outgoing one, and check the size each step. TC O(n), SC O(min(k, 26)).

followUps.q: s arrives as a streaming input of unknown length and you cannot store the whole string; report the count of good length-3 substrings seen so far.
followUps.a: Keep only the last two characters in a small buffer. When a new character arrives, you have a full window of three; run the same three pairwise checks, update the count, then shift the buffer. TC O(n), SC O(1).

followUps.q: Instead of length 3, count good substrings of length exactly n (the whole string must have all distinct characters).
followUps.a: Build a frequency array of size 26 while scanning; the moment any count exceeds 1 the answer is 0, otherwise it is 1. TC O(n), SC O(1).
